text:
anna: 👀 seeing a spike of GPU job failures after last night's base-image/toolkit rollout in us-west-2 and eu-west-1
mike: ugh, same. a bunch of training pods crash during init with libcuda errors
anna: example from worker-12 logs: 
```
Error: cannot load library libcuda.so.1: No such file or directory
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
RuntimeError: failed to create CUDA context
```
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollout completed: base-image:v2026.3.8 -> includes nvidia-container-toolkit 1.14.0
tasha: 1.14? we pinned to 1.13 for a reason (bind propagation oddities)
kevin: quick check: on an affected node, ls shows host has /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 but containers don't see it
mike: that sounds like a bind-propagation/namespace issue - toolkit usually mounts driver libs into container rootfs
anna: i grabbed `docker run --rm --gpus all ubuntu:22.04 ls -l /run/nvidia/driver || ls -l /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so*` from a node and it returns nothing inside the container
kevin: host: `ls -l /run/nvidia/driver/libcuda.so*` -> files present
tasha: possible regression in how our init script or toolkit config sets the mount propagation (rshared vs private)
anna: i also see a ton of NCCL WARNs shortly before failures: "NCCL WARN Call to cuGetProcAddress failed" (probably a symptom)
mike: region impact: ~12% of GPU capacity in us-west-2, ~8% in eu-west-1. Jobs started to fail ~3:40am UTC after image roll
sre-lead: impact acknowledged. prioritize rollback if remediation can't be applied in ~20m
kevin: quick mitigation we tested on one node: stop kubelet, remount with rshared, restart kubelet, then run `docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi` -> works
anna: commands we ran (on node): 
```
systemctl stop kubelet
mount --make-rshared /
# restart kubelet
systemctl start kubelet
# verify
docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base nvidia-smi
```
mike: not ideal to run mount --make-rshared globally during a live rollout without testing everywhere
tasha: alternative is patching our host-init container to explicitly bind /run/nvidia/driver into pods as a volume with propagation:rshared - that's lower blast radius and can be applied per-node via daemonset
infra-bot: incident-bot: created incident INF-2026-311 (GPU driver libs missing in containers) - severity: high
sre-lead: action items: 1) halt further rollout of base-image/toolkit 1.14 2) start rolling rollback to 1.13 on affected fleets 3) apply daemonset hotfix to bind /run/nvidia/driver with rshared for quick mitigation 4) schedule postmortem
kevin: i've started automated rollback job for us-west-2 canary pool
mike: creating a small pool of replacement nodes (with toolkit 1.13) and draining affected ones is safest for now
anna: note: some older kernels on our legacy GPU hosts (5.4) show slightly different behavior vs newer 5.15/6.x - need to include kernel matrix in postmortem
tasha: also verify image builds didn't change NVIDIA_LIBS_PATH or moved symlinks. 1.14 added a new path under /run/nvidia/driver rather than relying on earlier bind behavior
kevin: temporary script to detect affected nodes: 
```
if ! docker run --rm --gpus all nvidia/cuda:12.1-base ls /run/nvidia/driver 2>/dev/null | grep libcuda; then
  echo AFFECTED
fi
```
mike: i'm patching our autoscaler to stop provisioning new GPU nodes with toolkit 1.14 until rollback completes
sre-lead: communications: pinging support + customers with impacted SLAs. infra status page updated
anna: postmortem to include variance in mount propagation behavior across container runtimes (containerd vs dockerd), toolkit change log for 1.14, and test coverage gap for mount prop
tasha: for QA: add an integration test that runs `docker run --rm --gpus ...` on a fresh node with different kernel versions and with kubelet mount namespaces configured as we do in prod
kevin: rolling rollback ETA for us-west-2 canary: 14m
mike: i'm starting the eu-west-1 rollback now
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback base-image:v2026.3.7 -> completed on node pool gpu-canary-usw2-1
anna: can we also schedule a targeted restart of long-running pods so they pick up the fixed mounts? nodes we fix will be drained/restarted anyway
sre-lead: yes - drain, cordon, replace with fresh nodes. minimize job restarts by migrating running batch workloads first
tasha: after rollback we should still push the rshared daemonset patch as defense-in-depth
anna: thanks all — monitoring GPU job success rate. will update when rates return to normal
kevin: success metrics improving on canary, failures dropping to baseline
mike: eu-west rollback done, starting node replacement there
anna: marking this thread for the incident PM, will close when all affected nodes are rotated
infra-bot: incident-bot: INF-2026-311 severity downgraded to medium (progressing)
